tasks.title: Retrieve Argentina-Washington correspondence, 1921-1925
tasks.research_gap: Underlying Argentine diplomatic records have not been examined. They may locate the origin of the Daumas/Dumont attribution and document what Argentina transmitted to Washington.
tasks.collection: Embajada en Washington, Estados Unidos I (27.A)
tasks.critical_rule: Preserve Daumas, Dumont, or any other attribution exactly as written; do not normalize disputed names.
tasks.high_value_result: A dated Argentine-origin record identifying the sculptor, original work, fabrication or copy process, donor, or information formally transmitted to the U.S. government.

tasks.title: Retrieve Uruguay-Washington Artigas monument correspondence, 1947-1951
tasks.research_gap: Uruguay's diplomatic archive identifies a U.S. Embassy record series covering 1900-1990, but the underlying 1947-1951 correspondence has not been examined. It may establish the donor, fabrication and casting history, shipment, installation, dedication, and the precise relationship between the Washington statue and the Juan Luis Blanes Artigas model.
tasks.repository: Archivo Historico-Diplomatico, Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, Uruguay
tasks.collection: Sub Fondo Legaciones y Embajadas, 2.10 Embajada de la Republica en Estados Unidos (1900-1990)
priority_units: Request inventory/folder-level description for 1947-1951 before retrieval
tasks.critical_rule: Separate the Washington object's documented fabrication and casting from the authorship/model lineage. A later reproduction of the Juan Luis Blanes model does not make every fabricator or caster the sculptor.
tasks.high_value_result: A contemporaneous Uruguayan diplomatic or administrative record identifying who authorized, fabricated, cast, shipped, presented, or described the Washington Artigas statue and its relationship to the San Jose de Mayo model.

tasks.title: Retrieve the U.S. diplomatic spine for the Cuban Friendship Urn, 1926-1928
tasks.research_gap: The Cuban-side archival lineage is not assumed to be symmetrically recoverable. The immediate task is to reconstruct the preserved U.S. diplomatic spine and then test it against independently recoverable Cuban contemporary records. Unequal archival survival or access must not be treated as evidence that the better-preserved U.S. account is more truthful.
tasks.repository: National Archives and Records Administration, United States
tasks.collection: RG 59, General Records of the Department of State, 1910-29 Central Decimal File; USS Maine memorial in Cuba
priority_units: File 837.413M28/16 - Despatch No. 172, Noble Brandon Judah to Secretary of State, 10 Apr 1928
National Archives Microfilm Publication M488, roll 55 - entire file 837.413M28
Review surrounding 1926-1928 correspondence for fabrication, transfer, custody, ceremony and material-lineage statements
tasks.critical_rule: Separate ceremony/presentation, object identity, and material provenance into distinct propositions. A diplomatic record directly establishes what officials reported or did; it establishes reuse of memorial material only when the record contains sufficiently direct evidence for that proposition. Missing or inaccessible Cuban-side records are ARCHIVAL_GAP, not negative evidence.
tasks.high_value_result: Contemporaneous records that separately establish the 1928 transfer, identify the object, and document or directly trace the claimed reuse of material from the damaged Havana Maine memorial.

tasks.title: Recover an independent Cuban contemporary record lane for the Friendship Urn
tasks.research_gap: A Cuban contemporary evidentiary lane is needed to test the U.S. diplomatic account without assuming that a present-day Cuban diplomatic archive can provide a complete mirror collection. Remotely accessible newspapers, official publications, speeches, conference material, photographs, and digitized Cuban records should be sought as distinct source lineages.
tasks.repository: Multiple Cuban and international digitized repositories
tasks.collection: Contemporary Cuban newspapers, official publications, presidential or diplomatic texts, Sixth International Conference materials, and historical photographs, 1926-1928
priority_units: 1926 hurricane and damage to the Havana Maine memorial
Contemporary statements describing fabrication or material reuse
Historical images capable of documenting the memorial, fragments, urn, inscription, or ceremony
tasks.critical_rule: Classify newspaper and published records by origin where possible: original reporting, official-text reproduction, diplomatic release, wire copy, editorial, or unknown. Multiple reproductions of the same upstream statement remain one lineage. Do not infer absence of a Cuban record from failure to retrieve one online.
tasks.high_value_result: A Cuban-origin contemporary source independent of the U.S. State Department chain that confirms, contradicts, qualifies, or more precisely describes the urn's fabrication, material origin, presentation, or chain of custody.
